missing.usage: Used by surfers to describe large, powerful, hollow, or intimidating waves.
examples: Watch out on da outside, da heavies stay rolling in.

missing.usage: Being deep inside the hollow curve of a breaking wave or right in the heaviest spot of the impact zone.
examples: He wen drop in right in da pit!

missing.usage: Poor, blown-out, choppy, or unrideable wave conditions.
examples: Too much wind today, only get junk surf.

missing.usage: To surf or skate with high performance, throwing heavy carves and turns.
examples: Look at dat grom shred da gnar at Bowls!

missing.usage: A surf spot where waves peel along a point of land or reef headland.

missing.usage: Checking the surf or paddling out at the crack of dawn before crowds arrive.
examples: We go dawn patrol tomorrow at 5:30 AM.

missing.usage: When a wave crests and breaks entirely at one time across the reef with no open shoulder to ride.
examples: Every wave was one close out, couldn't make da shoulder.

missing.usage: Major surf etiquette violation where a surfer takes off on a wave in front of someone who already has right of way.

missing.usage: Hawaiian-style char siu pork bun, available steamed (traditional white) or baked, sold in local shops and manapua trucks.

missing.usage: Iconic Hawaii comfort dish: a bed of white rice topped with a hamburger patty, fried egg, and rich brown gravy.
examples: Gimme one loco moco with two eggs sunny side up.

english: seasoned raw fish bowl over rice

examples: I going buy one spicy ahi poke bowl fo' lunch.

missing.usage: Having an abundant, delicious spread of local food.
examples: Aunty wen cook choke grindz fo' da graduation party.

missing.usage: Pidgin slang for food or the act of eating.

missing.usage: Sweet, sour, and salty dried plum powder used to season gummy candies, fresh fruit (like pineapple and apples), or shave ice.

examples: Grab two spam musubi from 7-Eleven fo' da beach trip.

examples: We go drive-in get one chicken katsu plate lunch.

missing.usage: A Portuguese yeast doughnut fried until golden, coated in granulated sugar or cinnamon, and optionally filled with haupia or custard.

missing.usage: Finely shaved ice (not crushed) soaked in tropical flavored syrups, often served over vanilla ice cream with azuki beans and sweetened condensed milk (snow cap).

missing.usage: Traditional Hawaiian salted, seasoned, and sun-dried beef, often pan-fried before serving.
examples: Dat luau had ono pipikaula and poi.

missing.usage: Traditional Hawaiian coconut milk pudding, sliced into blocks or used as dessert pie/cake filling.

missing.usage: Hawaiian word meaning to slice or cut crosswise into pieces; refers to seasoned diced raw fish (usually yellowfin ahi).

missing.usage: Describes something physically damaged, a person who is exhausted/beaten up, or people laughing uncontrollably.

missing.usage: Describes someone who is being fake, disingenuous, or putting on a front.
examples: No act all fakafied, just be yourself.

missing.usage: A compliment praising someone for being dependable, true to their word, or doing a great favor.
examples: Thanks for picking me up at the airport, you solid bro.

missing.usage: Exclamation when someone looks extraordinarily fly, does a slick maneuver, or is showing off stylish flair.

missing.usage: Slang contraction of 'guaranteed'; means something is certain or promised.

missing.usage: Admonition telling someone not to act arrogant, show off in public, or make a fool of themselves.

missing.usage: Giving someone a dirty look or glaring with disapproval or irritation.

missing.usage: Getting goosebumps from emotional music, spooky ghost stories, or awe-inspiring moments.

missing.usage: Philosophical local phrase representing a relaxed, flexible attitude toward life and plans.

missing.usage: To speak negatively, gossip maliciously, or badmouth people behind their backs.

missing.usage: Describes someone who is sulking, grumpy, or throwing a silent tantrum because they didn't get their way.

english: go for a leisure drive or stroll
missing.usage: To go out exploring, driving, strolling, or visiting friends with no strict agenda.

missing.usage: Enthusiastic contraction of 'all right' used to express agreement, celebration, or excitement.

missing.usage: Local pronunciation of 'roger that' meaning affirmative, acknowledged, or agreed.

missing.usage: An outdoor porch, covered patio, or open-air veranda on a home or condo.
examples: Let's sit out on the lanai and drink coffee.

missing.usage: Cardinal direction in Hawaii meaning toward the mountains or inland (opposite of makai).
examples: Turn mauka at the next intersection.

missing.usage: Cardinal direction in Hawaii meaning toward the ocean or sea (opposite of mauka).
